newsitem.title: MEXICO: PEMEX SAYS PRODUCTION UNAFFECTED BY REFINERY BLAST.
newsitem.headline: PEMEX SAYS PRODUCTION UNAFFECTED BY REFINERY BLAST.

text.p: Mexico's oil monopoly said a blast at its Ciudad Madero refinery on Sunday night had no effect on production and left nine people injured, a spokeswoman from Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Tuesday.
The explosion at the Tamaulipas refinery was because of a pressure from a deposit of fuel oil, said the Pemex source, who declined to be named.
Nine contracted painters were injured in the blast, she added. Local newspaper reports said at least three of the workers were in "serious" condition.
The Gulf of Mexico coast refinery is the smallest of Mexico's six refineries with average 1995 output of 167,700 barrels per day of refined products.

Pemex also said in a statement there was a fire along its gasoline duct Tula-Azcapotzalco on Monday in an attempted gasoline theft. The blaze took four hours to contain and injured four people in a passing car, Pemex said.
